comments.subject: Mojave Crossing Hotel
comments.comment:
Dear City Recorder,

We urgently request that you stop this hotel from coming right next to our safe and quiet neighborhood as we feel it will be a disaster with noise, crime and undesirable people in our neighborhood. This has not been allowed to happen in other residential neighborhoods in St. George and it would be so wrong next to a 55 and older community. It doesn't matter how the hotel is placed on the lot, just being at that location is the same problem. A police officer spoke at the last meeting and told what a disaster it would be for us resident and he definitely knows the problems we would experience. Please do not let this hotel or any hotel come into that lot and area.

Thank you for your prompt attention,
Marae and John Holman

comments.subject: Mojave Crossing project
comments.comment:
FYI: City Recorder Re: message to City Council, December 29, 2024

My wife and I are residents of SunRiver in the area immediately adjacent the proposed Mojave Junction project that is intended to place a 24/7 hotel butted up against our neighborhood.

Our purpose is to urge you to vote against this project. Many reasons have already been described before the the Planning Commission. This proposed hotel cannot be equivalently compared to the Hampton Inn and Suites and the new planned Home2 by Hilton is perfectly located.

The Mojave Junction hotel is located right against the SunRiver neighborhood with no buffer. It will provide noise and traffic and likely invasive light to the homes near it which will be disturbing to the SunRiver residents.

Also to be considered is the traffic and parking on Sandpiper Drive, a neighborhood thoroughfare where residents walk with dogs, exercise and ride their bicycles. Parking there is likely since the planned hotel has inadequate parking planned for the buildings foreseen especially the hotel.

Safety for residents is a huge consideration due to the proximity to the neighborhood and its 55+ vulnerable residents and the transient population that will use the hotel. Opportunity is enhanced for would-be criminals because of that location and its proximity.

For that area, it simply is not a good idea and we encourage you again to please oppose it.

Respectfully,
Derek and Linda Shubin

comments.subject: Mojave Hotel
comments.comment:
We are full-time residents of Sun River. Our home is just down the block from where the proposed hotel will be. We are NOT happy about this development AT ALL. We moved here to be in a quiet, peaceful 55+ community and this hotel will encroach on the benefits of that. We do not want the traffic, the noise, or the higher probability of crime.

We ask that you PLEASE do not approve this hotel. It would really bring a negative impact to our community down here.

Thank you,
Bonnie and Steve Burnett

comments.subject: Please vote NO on the 107 unit Mojave Crossing Hotel
comments.comment:
Please, vote NO on the Mojave Crossing Hotel at your Thursday meeting. The other two projects, the medical office and the retail buildings, are fine. But a 107 unit 3 story hotel does NOT fit in this neighborhood. As you travel across the country you seldom see a 3 story hotel in an established neighborhood of senior citizens. The 3 story hotel will cause privacy issues with the home owners on Painted Finch Drive.

We already have a Hampton Inn and a Hilton is coming in just east of Pioneer Road. The Sun River is a 55+ community with many citizen driving golf carts around the Smith's store. The added traffic and noise the hotel will bring will make a serious safety issue for our senior citizens. Please vote NO on the Mojave Crossing 107 unit hotel.

Keith & Janine Grebe

comments.subject: Mojave Crossing Commercial Development
comments.comment:
Dear Mayor Randall,

Please deny the proposed hotel. I support retail and medical/professional service businesses, but I do not support the hotel at this location. I strongly object to a hotel adjacent to the SunRiver Community. The proposed location is too close to our vulnerable elderly population. Data proves that hotels increase property crime and violent crime in surrounding areas. Allowing a hotel in the Mojave Crossing development would damage the surrounding community.

A hotel will disrupt the peaceful nature of our neighborhood and create traffic safety concerns. Parking is still inadequate. The design does not accommodate RVs, trailers, or larger trucks due to tight turns and space requirements. Additionally, the code requires only two employee parking spaces, yet similar hotels, such as the Hampton Inn, employ up to 30 workers during peak times. This will result in overflow parking on Sand Piper Drive, which borders residential backyards, creating safety and privacy concerns.

Additionally, the buffer zones are still insufficient to ensure the safety and well-being of nearby residents. Any project at this location should include a right-turn-only exit onto Sand Piper Drive. And please restrict trash collection hours to between 7:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m.

Please prevent the negative impact and unintended consequences of a hotel in our neighborhood.

Thank you for your service to our city.

Sincerely,
Jonathan Kreisle

comments.subject: Mojave Hotel Project
comments.comment:
Sunriver retirement community members concerns. Our concerns for Sunriver community members.

I'm personally opposed to a hotel across the street from where I live for the following reasons:

1) We are a retirement community and moved to Sunriver for peace and quiet!
2) Hotels operate 24 hours a day, 365 days a year.
3) Nowhere in the city of St. George is there a hotel behind residential homes.
4) Hotels belong in business areas or downtown where there is easy access to those services.
5) Hotels in your backyard looking into your windows and backyard areas takes away our privacy. Parking of boats, trailers, motor homes and oversized trucks that can't park in hotel parking will park on sandpiper road behind our homes.
6) Lights, noise and activity at all hours of the day and night will disrupt your privacy, safety, right of enjoyment and peace.
7) Hotels will bring strangers to our easy access street (walkers, runners, door knockers, strangers taking away our privacy)
8) The Development Monitoring Committee gave input on a hotel in our neighborhood and the developer ignored our input

Thank you for your time
John & Debbie Vasquez

comments.subject: MOJAVE CROSSING (HOTEL)
comments.comment:
As resident homeowner's at SunRiver:

We do not support the Hotel location being placed among the retail and Medical/Professional Service Businesses.

The revised plan now meets the City's Setback requirements but I think the buffer zones are still insufficient to ensure the safety and well-being of nearby residents.

The Planning Staff has determined the parking plan meets requirements under City Code 10-19-7, which allows for a "shared" parking concept of which is believed to be inadequate. Additionally, the code requires only two employee parking spaces, yet similar hotels, such as the Hampton Inn, employ up to 30 workers during peak times. This will result in overflow parking concerns.

Trash Pickup - Planning Staff recommends restricting trash collection between 6:00 am and 8:00 pm. This restriction must remain in place as it was previously applied for the Patio Furniture [...]

Residents in the road area of Sandpiper Drive requested consideration of a right-turn-only exit onto Nighthawk Drive in order to help reduce traffic volumes and prevent delivery trucks from driving [behind residences]. Planning Commission did not and it is no longer a part of the projection. There doesn't appear to be any particular reason why the Planning Commission rejected this and ask you all to reconsider.

Thank you,
James and Linda Young

comments.subject: Mojave Crossing Development
comments.comment:
Mayor Randell and Councilmembers:

As residents of the SunRiver community we have significant concerns about the Mojave Crossing development project that is currently being proposed. We feel the Mojave project is contrary to the City's original vision for the Atkinville Interchange and the vision established by SunRiver. We are requesting that the City deny this project.

It appears the portion of the Atkinville Interchange that lies EAST of I-15 has been approved for "Visitor/Convenience Commercial zoned for "Visitor-oriented businesses such as convenience stores,...LODGING..." However, properties WEST of I-15 / East of Pioneer Road is zoned a mix of retail/commercial/residential, designed to create a convenient, enjoyable environment for shopping, dining, and/or obtaining personal services with "retail and commercial services for LOCAL RESIDENTS..."

We know that many of our SunRiver friends and neighbors purchased homes based on the "original" Atkinville and SunRiver visions. We would definitely support development aligning with the Atkinville Interchange vision that would provide goods and service type businesses while prioritizing the safety and well-being of SunRiver's aging population.

At the time we purchased our SunRiver property - which is located very near the location of the proposed hotel- we felt we would be making a stable real estate investment. We were impressed that the original vision for the residential area was one that deemed itself to be a walkable, bikeable, golf cart resort-style community with abundant amenities for retirees.

The SunRiver vision focused on peaceful, safe living with community support. Interesting that the City's own General Plan also emphasizes livability, safety, and walkability for seniors.

Those visions seem to be eroding before our eyes ...but the City now has an opportunity to uphold and protect the original intended visions for development adjacent to our retirement community. You can start by denying the Mojave project.

Why would the City allow certain types of uses so close to homes of vulnerable citizens? The primary responsibility of any city council is to ensure the safety and well-being of its residents.

The SunRiver community would surely be negatively impacted by this proposed change.

We are primarily concerned about the following:
- this hotel would lack a sufficient buffer zone from residential areas.
- Safety is compromised when transient populations are this close to vulnerable seniors.
- Hotels enable community crimes of opportunity which can be high-risk to elderly citizens.
- 24/365 operations result in noise, light pollution, and increased traffic-all detrimental to nearby residences.
- The project lacks clear guarantees on ownership and management quality.
- Potential future uses (e.g., low-end brands or subsidized housing) could further erode community quality.
- Overflow parking will spill onto Sand Piper Dr and Nighthawk Dr which residents utilize for bicycling/walking to access the Aspiration Trail Trailhead raising safety concerns.
- Overflow parking will butt up against homes and entrances into the community raising safety concerns.

We would also like to add the following recommendations:
- We support the retail and medical/professional service business, but we strongly suggest that you do not support the hotel at this location
- We encourage you to state that the buffer zones are still insufficient to ensure the safety and well-being of nearby residents
- We do not think that parking is adequate. The design does not accommodate RV's, trailers or larger trucks due to tight turns. The limited employee parking is also inadequate and will likely result in parking on Sandpiper Drive, which borders residential back yards, creating safety and privacy concerns.
- Restriction of trash collection hours to between 8:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m.
- We request a right-turn only exit onto Nighthawk Drive to reduce traffic volume and prevent delivery trucks from driving behind residents homes.

We respectfully urge the City to prioritize the safety and integrity of our 55+ community by denying this project on the basis that it is incompatible with the adjoining community and conflicts with the Atkinville Interchange and SunRiver.

Sincerely,
Dan & Michaelene Rowe

comments.contact_name: Col. and Mrs. Bruce Barnes (Bruce and Catherine Barnes)
comments.subject: Opposition to Building of Hotel in SunRiver (Mojave Crossing Project)
comments.comment:
Dear Mayor Randall:

According to the Planning Commission's September 10th follow-up meeting and project-detailed changes resulting therefrom, we hereby submit this updated email in support of the email previously sent in June 2024 to Monica Smith, outlining our concerns and continued Strong Opposition to the building of a hotel that has no identifying brand ("Proposed Hotel") in the SunRiver Location ("SR Location"), and ask that it be added to our record and included in the decision-making process.

Building Site Adjustments (Hotel, Retail, Medical/Professional):

WE STRONGLY SUPPORT the part of the Mojave Crossing Development Project ("Mojave Project") that involves construction of the retail and medical/professional service businesses for the SR Location.

WE STRONGLY OPPOSE the part of the Mojave Project that involves construction of the Proposed Hotel for the SR Location to include, but not limited to, the following Community Safety Risks and Operations and Long-Term Concerns.
- Unlike other St. George hotels, the Proposed Hotel DOES NOT support a sufficient buffer zone (between residential and commercial properties) to ensure the safety and well-being of its nearby residents.
- Safety is often compromised when transient people are close to vulnerable elderly citizens.
- Hotels typically lead to increased crime. The proximity of the Proposed Hotel to SunRiver's 55+ Retirement Community would not only seriously jeopardize the safety and security of our community's elderly citizens, but also raise significant concerns about the overall safety of our community.
- The Proposed Hotel's 24-hour-daily operational hours and constant influx of guests will intensify the noise, light pollution, and increased traffic in the SR Location, all detrimental to elderly residents living nearby.
- The Mojave Project has not identified either the brand of the Proposed Hotel or the management team that would run it. This lack of transparency regarding the Proposed Hotel's ownership and management concerns all SunRiver residents.
- Excerpted from an NBC News report (12/25/2024) regarding residents in Kingston, NY: "Due to a surge in rents and home prices, many lower-income residents are being forced out of their homes and seeking shelter in hotels because it has become the only viable option for them to turn to for their living situation. This leads to subsidized and/or long-term housing, ultimately eroding the value of the community. The above situation is happening elsewhere as well."

As SunRiver residents we oppose any action which enables/promotes the erosion of our retirement community and compromises our safety.

St. George City's Buffer Zones: Although St. George City's revised plan regarding buffer zones meets the setback requirements according to its zoning laws and regulations, these zones are still insufficient to ensure the safety and well-being of nearby residents because of the Proposed Hotel's proximity to the SR Location.

Parking Concerns/Safety and Privacy Issues: St. George City's design for the Proposed Hotel parking is inadequate and DOES NOT accommodate for oversized vehicles such as RVs, trailers or larger trucks making narrow turns in its parking spaces. Additionally, the code requires the Proposed Hotel to have only two (2) employee parking spaces when similar hotels employ up to 30 employees during peak times. This shortage will certainly result in overflow parking on Sand Piper Drive, which borders residential backyards, thereby leading to safety and privacy concerns for its residents.

Trash Pickup: WE SUPPORT the Planning staff's recommendation that trash collection hours be scheduled between 8:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m. ONLY, so that the area's residents can maintain the peaceful and tranquil enjoyment of their homes.

Sand Piper Drive - Right-Turn Exit Only: WE SUPPORT the Planning staff's request that ANY project surrounding Sand Piper Drive and Nighthawk Drive include a Right-Turn-Only Exit onto Nighthawk Drive. This requirement will reduce traffic volume and prevent delivery trucks from driving behind residential homes, which could ultimately lead to safety and privacy issues.

TO SUMMARIZE: SunRiver advocates for responsible development that aligns with St. George City's values. The St. George General Plan emphasizes the vision of SunRiver, a community where residents can walk, run, ride bikes, and drive their golf carts without fearing for their safety. This vision is not just a dream, but a shared value with which the entire community supports and aligns. The Mojave Project, on the other hand, DOES NOT support and DOES NOT align with this vision.

The SunRiver community recognizes that St. George's growth necessitates change, which also must factor in proper zoning as part of the change. The City Council's primary responsibility is to prioritize its residents' safety and well-being. While the SunRiver community supports development that benefits residents and developers, it should NEVER BE at the expense of community safety and well-being. We are advocates for responsible development, and we believe that this can be achieved without compromising our safety.

A safe community fosters trust and stability that supports St. George's local economy, property values, and a general high quality of life for all its residents. Zoning decisions that do not fully consider safety concerns can ultimately lead to long-term problems, especially for elderly and vulnerable residents. Neglecting safety in the Mojave Project could lead to such problems, which we must all strive to avoid.

FINAL REQUEST TO DENY HOTEL: As residents of SunRiver, we respectfully urge all of you involved with the Mojave Crossing Development Project to consider and prioritize the safety, integrity, and well-being of the SunRiver residents when making your decision to either approve or disapprove of the Proposed Hotel portion of the Mojave Project. Approving this portion would significantly compromise our community's safety. Therefore, we urge you to DENY only the Proposed Hotel portion of the Mojave Crossing Development Project for the SunRiver Location.

Thank you for taking the time to hear our concerns.

Bruce Barnes
Catherine Barnes
SunRiver Homeowners

comments.subject: Mohave Crossing - Approve Medical/Professional & Retail Space - Disapprove Hotel
comments.comment:
Dear Mayor Randall:

We are writing to express our support for the proposed medical/professional office space and the retail space at the Mohave Crossing development. However, we strongly oppose the plan to build a hotel (one of the three-tiers of the Mojave Crossing Development Project), slated to be built on the lot next to SunRiver (between Sand Piper Dr. and Pioneer Dr., and adjacent to Nighthawk Dr.).

Issue 1. Wrong Location for a Hotel or any 24/7 Operation - We moved to SunRiver three years ago from North Carolina (Air Force Retirees) and have been very happy here. This was our 20th move, and we don't intend to move again. We've lived in many places around the country - nowhere has there been a hotel or any other 24/7 operation so close to a residential development. Hotels have been documented to correlate with increased crime rates (i.e., burglary, theft, assault, drugs, human trafficking, and homicide) in the surrounding areas. Placing such a facility in close proximity to SunRiver's 55+ Retirement Community would seriously jeopardize the safety and security of our community's residents. The proximity of the hotel to our 55+ aged community homes is too close despite the revised site plan for the lot in question. This is not a location for a hotel or any other 24/7 operation no matter how much of an offset is built-in with sidewalks, streets, and landscaping. The transient nature of the business brings people to the area that have no investment in the community and are just too close to vulnerable aged individuals. The appropriate location for a hotel is on the east side of Pioneer Road, sufficiently removed from the residential homes.

Issue 2. Safety and Noise - Building a hotel or other 24/7 operation in our location would disrupt the peaceful living that drew us to SunRiver. The 24/7 operational hours of the hotel and constant influx of guests will exacerbate noise and safety concerns and significantly disturb the peace and tranquility that attracted many of the residents to SunRiver. It will have a definite negative effect on property values and result in decreased property tax revenues from the SunRiver community. We agree with the recommendation that trash collection for anything developed on this lot be limited to the hours of 8:00 am-6:00 pm - no overnight or early morning collection for businesses.

Issue 3. Parking and Traffic - The revised site design for the development does not provide sufficient parking and will result in overflow parking on Sand Piper Drive, which borders residential backyards, creating significant safety and privacy concerns. The design does not accommodate RVs, trailers or large trucks that require a wide turning radius. Consequently, these large vehicles will end up being parked on Sand Piper Drive, immediately adjacent to the SunRiver residences. The design uses shared parking between businesses and only factors in two employee parking spaces for the hotel. This is insufficient - we know from experience that the Hampton Inn & Suites has up to 30 employees onsite during peak times. Hotel employees will also end up being parked on Sand Piper Drive. We strongly recommend that the traffic out of this development be directed to a right-turn-only exit onto Nighthawk Drive, directing traffic away from the SunRiver residences.

We urge the St. George City Council to modify the proposed Mohave Crossing development by doing the following:
1. Disapprove the construction of a hotel or any other 24/7 operation on this site
2. Approve the construction of medical/professional space and retail space with recommended traffic and parking accommodations.

We understand that the property's zoning laws allow a hotel to be built here. However, we firmly believe a hotel is completely inappropriate for this SunRiver neighborhood. It is crucial that the St. George City Council understand the depth of the SunRiver community opposition to building this hotel here. The area would be much better suited to a combination of medical/professional offices and retail space. As such, when making your decision, we urgently implore that all of you involved please consider the well-being and wishes of the SunRiver residents.

Thank you, Mayor Randall, and to all others involved with the St. George City Council in the decision making of the proposed hotel at the Mohave Crossing development, for taking the time to review our concerns and strong opposition to the hotel, which will ultimately be detrimental to the SunRiver location. We trust that all of you will make the right decision to prioritize our community's safety and quality of life that we presently enjoy over any commercial interests that do not align with our residential location.

Thank you for your time.

Brent & Cindy Erickson

comments.subject: January 2, 2025 - Atikinville Interchange - Hotel project
comments.comment:
Regarding: 5. Consider approval of Ordinance No. 2025-001 amending 5.06 acres of the Atkinville Interchange Area Commercial PD-C for a 107-room hotel, a 23,000 square foot medical...

Over the past six years I have been part of the Sunriver community working with developers to find positive solutions to Development in the SunRiver / Atkinville Interchange. We have developed many positive relationships and I hope to see more collaboration for services that would meet the needs of our growing city. Unfortunately, we have discovered the zoning was changed in (2018) that would allow hotels and any other businesses that would operate 24 hrs/day 7 days/week "east of Pioneer" offers a quiet zone and buffer to residents that would experience greater safety and security to all residents of Sunriver. Building west of Pioneer would be detrimental to the Residents of SunRiver. The concerns include: parking, safety, security, noise, right of privacy, etc.

I was very surprised to see an officer of the Law (who was not part of the Sunriver residents at the meeting) stand up and speak to the Planning Commission regarding the hotel. He stated this would be a safety and security problem for the 55 Plus community (please read his transcript from the meeting).

I believe that Parking was not given due to consideration that would be necessary for this hotel. This would leave the city streets to be used for large vehicles, towing recreational toys, worker trailers, semi trailers and people traveling with multiple vehicles. These vehicles would end up lining Sand Piper Dr, due to the entry and exit along Sand Piper Dr.

SPECIAL Considerations: The Planning Commission asked the Mohave developer to rotate their hotel 90 degrees to prevent the hotel rooms from looking into our backyards - while this is a positive step, it's still not enough. There is no need for entry/exit on Sand Piper Dr, many commercial businesses have one entry/exit and this should only be on Pioneer Rd. In addition there should be a 6 foot wall on Sand Piper Dr further shielding the residential area and preventing all types of parking that would be disruptive to the Residents. This wall should also include part or all of NightHawk and perhaps even on the southside, if this property. The trash storage area would be better suited on the Southeast corner of the property away from any disruption while trash when being picked up, it would reduce the foul odors and noise.

My last concern is if this hotel is approved, we could easily see a number of Hotels built on the property between the Mojave hotel and the Fire Station. This would be extremely detrimental to SunRiver's quiet enjoyment, safety and security of our community. In addition, this would provide for "no/zero" community services to the residents of SunRiver. My reasoning for this statement is the owners of these properties have had them up for sale for over 8 years with few buyers. The property is being sold at three times the price of property in Desert Color. It seems this makes the only profitable businesses that could be developed in my backyard to be hotel's.

Sunriver has worked to the benefit of all with a number of developers in our area to support and come up with reasonable solutions to address concerns. We look forward to many more businesses that would serve our community and those at the southern end of St George! (Smith's, Les Schwab, Del Taco and we hear In & Out, StarBucks, Cafe Rio, a Hotel east of Pioneer and others yet to come and are excited to see them in our neighborhood)

Please do all you can to protect the Residents of SunRiver St. George Community Association.

Thank you for reading my suggestions and concerns. Thank you for your service to our great city of St. George!

Steve Lindley

comments.subject: Mojave Crossing Hotel
comments.comment:
As a resident of Sunriver St. George, I'm respectfully asking you to not allow the Mojave Crossing hotel between Sandpiper Drive and Pioneer Road to be built in this location. This is not a place for a motel of this type, motels belong on the other side of the freeway or on the other side of Pioneer Road. There's a great deal of space by the convention center that would accommodate numerous hotels and restaurants. Hotels and restaurants in that area would encourage people to visit St. George and spend money at the convention center and other places throughout the city. This location does not have enough parking for customers, especially customers with large trucks, RVs and trailers. They will have no choice but to park on Sandpiper rd. This will cause this area of the Sunriver development to experience excess noise and disruption.

Also, this location does not provide green space for dog walking. Residents of the hotel will have no other place to walk their dogs other than along sandpiper as well as in our neighborhoods. The HOA pays for the maintenance of the green space along Sandpiper. Residents of the motel will walk their dogs in all likelihood will not pick up after themselves. We have common areas of green space in this neighborhood and people have personal green space in this yards. It will be hard pressed to get people to clean up after their dogs.

We are elderly people living in a very quiet area. This will be very disruptive to people, wanting to ride our bikes and walk our dogs along Sandpiper and feel safe. With all that's going on now in the world and the United States we don't feel safe. This will only Add to our stress. Please do not allow this Mojave Crossing hotel to be built in this location.

Thank you,
Larry Gillham
Lot 2162

comments.subject: Mojave crossing
comments.comment:
I am a retired Air Force Colonel and college teacher. My wife and I bought in SunRiver a year ago because of the classy layout of the community and well accomplished residents from all walks of life.
My concerns about the development and breach of plans is well stated by Karen Fisher. Don't screw this up, particularly the motel, parking and overflow.
We regret having to experience the city catering to developers. We insist on a safe and respected place to live.

comments.subject: Hotel Mojave Crossing Development & SunRiver Vulnerability
comments.comment:
Dear Mayor and team,
I am a resident of SunRiver and love it here, and southern utah. I actually raised my children in St. George and moved to Sun River 2 years ago because I love living in our beautiful city.

I am concerned about the planned build of this Hotel near Exit 2 and so close to SunRiver. I'm concerned about the type of people it may attract to our peaceful neighborhood, as well as the amount of traffic. I'm concerned that the amount of crime in our neighborhood will increase because of the proximity to SunRiver. SunRiver is filled with older adults, that can be seduced by door to door scams, burglary, lack of alarm systems, the residents trusting of others (as they were raised) and other vulnerabilities.

I believe there are other parts of our county that would be more appropriate for this type of hotel. Please consider NOT building the Hotel at Mojave Crossing.

Sincerely,
Leanne Peterson

comments.subject: MOJAVE CROSSING
comments.comment:
Email: Monica.Smith@sgcity.org sent for September Planning Meeting held Sep 10, 2024

Dear Monica Smith,

Subject: COMMERCIAL DEVELOPMENT - MOJAVE CROSSING (NEW) Case No. 2024-PDA-009

My name is Nolan Costley and I live in SunRiver at 4157 S Painted Finch Dr. It has come to my attention that a developer (who has ignored our Community Development Committee suggestions) is seeking approval for a hotel/ long stay hotel on property adjacent to my address.

I am personally opposed to this addition so close to our residence. We have lived here for five years and moved here because of its serenity.

Several items immediately surface and need to be called to your attention:
- Hotels operate 24 hours a day, 7 days a week all year long.
- Location - this is a residential area for 55+ residents.
- This hotel is located right across the street from our home.
- Noise, traffic and lights - all hours of the day and night - these items will be a nuisance to our wellbeing.
- Safety - this will bring many people into our community that have no concern for us or our property.
- Is this the proper location for a hotel?
- Our yards and our homes will have no privacy because of this addition.
- Road safety - our movement around our community on our local streets will be impeded.

We love our SunRiver community and want to maintain its pristine environment we have come to enjoy so much.

Thanks for listening,
Nolan Costley

Amended December 29, 2024: I am amending this Email with additional information that concerns me after the Planning Commission approved the revised Mojave Crossing plan and sent it to the City Council.
- I can support the retail/medical use, but the hotel should be rejected for the above-mentioned reasons.
- I feel that the buffer zones are not adequate to ensure the safety and well-being of nearby residents.
- I feel that shared parking is also inadequate and will spill out onto the adjacent roads, creating unsafe situations for the local residents. Hotel users who drive large rigs will also park on the street - big problem for us. I encourage you to support your fellow residents in this area by rejecting the hotel.
- Trash pickup time must remain between 8:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m. Please support us on this matter.
- I feel the traffic exiting onto Sandpiper from this development should not be allowed to turn left but should be right hand turn only to keep traffic from flowing into the SunRiver community.

Thanks for your service with the City Council and listening to my concerns.
Regards Nolan Costley

comments.subject: Mohave Crossing Hotel
comments.comment:
Dear Mayor Randall and City Council:

I am writing to ask you to deny the request to build the proposed hotel at Mojave Crossing. The project is too big and does not provide enough of a buffer between the residential and commercial properties here in Sun River.

Please note that we are not against general development of the area. We currently have a Hampton Inn, and there is a sign for a proposed Home 2 hotel near Mojave Crossing. Those hotels are properly located in a commercial area, and there is a buffer zone between them and our Sun River neighborhood.

Throughout the process, we have felt that our voices are not being heard, which is very frustrating and leads less trust in our city government. Please vote against the hotel portion of this project.

Sincerely,
Stanley Eastman
St. George, Utah

comments.subject: Mojave Crossing Hotel Matter

Have a commercial property (hotel) directly behind residential property, would be considered an invasion of privacy due to being multiple stories and able to see in the privacy of private homes. Having Commerical property directly behind Residential houses could have a negative effect on the resale market of the houses as well as the negative effect on the values due to the location near commercial property. Hope this will be taken into account for this matter of allowing a hotel near residential houses.

Sincerely,
Debbie Swanson
Sun River

comments.subject: Planned Hotels on Pioneer

I have attached a list of hotels in St George, please note that the majority are not adjacent to residential communities. I have also attached research results for hotel related crime and other issues.

These hotels are a bad mix for a senior community. If this is allow to progress Sun River residents will do everything possible to vote out irresponsible council members.

Stephen Sarchett
St George
